verses.verse:
षष्ठांशात् षष्ठमम् भागम् न्यूनंकृत्वा तु धैवतः।
अखण्डिते तु षष्ठांशे धैवतः षष्ठमे मतः।51।
verses.text: Dhaivata [is placed] after taking a sixth part away from the ṣaṣṭhāṃśa (one-sixth); but when the sixth is left undivided, Dhaivata is held to be at the [full] sixth.

commentary.text: If mandra Pañcama is open in the flute, then for the distance of Dhaivata, that is the first hole, above it: divide the ṣaṣṭhāṃśa (one-sixth) again into six parts, take one part away from it, and mark Dhaivata at whatever distance remains. Then, when making the hole, make it a small hole and enlarge it while testing the note. If Pañcama is not open but is made by a hole, the ṣaṣṭhāṃśa will remain whole.

But if the distance of the open Pañcama from the mouth-hole is nine 'miti', Dhaivata will be at the distance of the full ṣaṣṭhāṃśa (one-sixth). Take miti to mean paridhimāna (measure of the inner circumference).
